messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - multi-region failover anomaly detected for prod. Traffic-shift task 'rx-traffic-rehome' partially applied. Elevated 5xx and increased cross-region latency. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/multi-region-failover
emma.c: oncall here, seeing alerts from canary and synthetic checks in eu-west-1. Route53 weighted records show weights updated but some legacy weights are still resolving to us-east endpoints.
raj: confirmed. DNS queries from our probe fleet show split responses across global resolvers -> some clients still get us-east IPs (old weight) while traffic intended for eu routed correctly. TTL was 300s during the shift.
lee: adding context: traffic-shift job tried to move 100% of traffic to eu-west but encountered an error applying session-affinity bypass on the proxy group, so some proxies kept sticky cookies pointing at us-east origin. That created a routing mismatch.
netops: provider API reported a transient rate-limit on Route53 changes at 2001123502 which likely left the change partially committed. Case opened with provider.
pagerduty-bot: @emma.c acknowledged. ETA 3m.
emma.c: immediate mitigation: start targeted rollback to pre-shift weights for prod.example.com and open emergency short TTL (30s) to accelerate convergence. raj, can you run the Route53 weight-set job with force-apply?
raj: running force apply now: `./tools/r53-set --zone prod.example.com --record weighted --weights-file weights_pre_shift.json --force`
opsbot: executed job id=3721, started at 2001123528, stdout: "applied 3/4 records, 1 failed: rate limit"
lee: the failed record is the us-east failover alias. That explains partial routing. I'll retry with exponential backoff and smaller batch windows.
netops: also notice BGP flap between colo peers in eu-west-1 at 2001123490 which caused some edge POPs to prefer us-east for a short window. We've escalated to provider NOC.
emma.c: customer impact tracker updated: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2001123456 - approx 18% of API requests experienced < 10s increased latency, ~6% saw 5xx. Dedicated customers behind reserved endpoints saw more errors due to sticky sessions. No data corruption reported.
raj: retried apply with backoff, all Route53 weighted records now applied at 2001123560. Setting TTL to 30s.
lee: forcing proxy affinity override across the edge pool `edge-conf set session_affinity=none --scope=prod --duration=5m` to avoid old cookies holding traffic to us-east.
opsbot: proxy change rolled: change-id=chg-8234, started 2001123576, completed 2001123585.
emma.c: starting a controlled canary: 2% traffic to eu-west endpoints, monitoring error budget.
raj: canary metrics: no increased 5xx in canary. Moving to 25% at 2001123600.
lee: at 25% we see a small uptick in backend timeouts from a subset of proxies that still had stale keepalive connections. I'm issuing a rolling restart of those proxies to drop stale connections.
netops: provider updated NOC: BGP flap resolved in eu-west-1 at 2001123612, no further flaps.
opsbot: rolling restart command: `kubectl rollout restart ds/proxy-edge -l region=eu-west-1 -n redwood-edge` (started 2001123618)
emma.c: after restart and DNS convergence, error rate trending down. 5xx back to baseline within 180s of final change.
raj: note: some clients with long DNS caches (ISP-level) will still hit us-east IPs until their resolver evicts entries. We'll keep a temporary routing shim in us-east that returns 200 by proxying to eu-west to reduce customer-visible errors.
lee: shim implemented (`edge-shim`), proxies in us-east now perform HTTP reverse-proxy to eu-west for the affected host header - reduces cross-region latencies for those clients. Deployed at 2001123650.
emma.c: initiating handoff: @raj will own follow-up until 22:00 UTC. I'll write initial timeline. Handoff notes: ensure runbook updated for partial Route53 commit behavior and add safety to traffic-shift to poll provider-change status and verify all record sets applied.
netops: recommend change: reduce TTL to 60s during any weighted routing shifts and implement a pre-flight check on provider rate limits. Also add BGP health as a gating signal for full-region failover.
opsbot: ACTION CREATED: INC-2001123456-POSTMORTEM - owner=raj, due=2001127056.
pagerduty-bot: @raj assigned for post-incident tasks.
emma.c: can someone paste relevant logs for the proxy errors?
lee: logs snippet:
```
proxy-edge 2026-08-12T14:12:34Z [warn] upstream timeout after 10s for 10.20.30.15: connect timed out
edge-shim 2026-08-12T14:12:46Z [info] proxied request host=prod.example.com -> eu-west-1:200 OK
```
raj: running summary of root-cause hypotheses: 1) Route53 rate-limit left weighted records partially applied, 2) session-affinity bypass failed on subset of proxies causing sticky routing to old region, 3) transient BGP flap nudged some POPs to prefer us-east. Composite failure produced split-brain routing and elevated errors.
emma.c: plan: immediate fixes already applied (force Route53 apply, reduced TTL, affinity override, proxy restart, edge shim). Next steps in postmortem: add provider-rate-limit handling, implement traffic-shift verification step that queries global resolvers for record convergence, add a full-region force-failover toggle that bypasses sticky sessions.
lee: I'll own change to proxy agent to add `--drain-sticky` flag that actively rewrites cookies for sessions during failover.
netops: follow-up with provider around rate-limits and BGP root cause. Case id: PRV-99812.
opsbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring (2001123690). Will close when metrics stable for 30m and postmortem posted.
emma.c: thanks team. Great fast coordination. I'll schedule the incident review meeting for 2001124000 UTC and assign notes to @raj.
